sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) follows a client-host-server architecture where each host can run multiple client instances [E1][E4]. MCP is open and enables integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools [E12][E23]. The DuckDB MCP server is distributed via the mcp-server-motherduck package. Install it using uv (preferred for Python CLI tools) or pip [E8]. The server acts as a bridge between DuckDB and AI-driven environments, such as Cursor or Claude, allowing these tools to execute SQL commands and return results in real time. It supports both local DuckDB instances and cloud-based MotherDuck databases [E10]. Rill's default embedded engine is DuckDB [E27]. Rill Developer is an open-source, code-first BI tool that enables software engineers to profile data sets, design data models, and deploy dashboards to Rill Cloud [E31]. Users will follow the same basic steps that include downloading and installing Rill, configuring MotherDuck as a source, entering a SQL expression to return a single table and clicking import [E39][E40]. Together, these components allow AI assistants to query DuckDB databases and surface results in Rill-powered dashboards [E13][E30].

sections.heading: Concepts
sections.body: MCP follows a client-host-server architecture with stateful sessions; each client connects to exactly one server [E3][E6][E23]. Servers expose resources, tools, and prompts via MCP primitives [E7][E23]. The server acts as a bridge between DuckDB and AI-driven environments, such as Cursor or Claude, allowing these tools to execute SQL commands and return results in real time. It supports both local DuckDB instances and cloud-based MotherDuck databases [E10]. The DuckDB/MotherDuck MCP server allows the AI copilot (Cursor) to directly run queries against local DuckDB databases and/or remote MotherDuck databases and interpret the results [E13]. This guide assumes you'll be using Rill's default embedded engine, DuckDB [E27]. Rill Developer is an open-source, code-first BI tool that enables software engineers to profile data sets, design data models, and deploy dashboards to Rill Cloud [E31]. By default, Rill includes DuckDB as an embedded OLAP engine that ingests data from data sources and powers your dashboards. When you start a new project, you'll see a connectors/duckdb.yaml file alongside other project files. No additional configuration is needed to use DuckDB with Rill Developer or Rill Cloud [E36]. Because Rill is already built with DuckDB embedded, no additional type wrangling is needed, the data in MotherDuck is "production-ready" for Rill dashboards [E41]. MCP primitives (tools, prompts, resources) connect AI models to external data [E23][E25][E26].

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Install the DuckDB MCP server with uv pip install mcp-server-motherduck or pip install mcp-server-motherduck [E8]. Configure an IDE such as Cursor by adding a JSON entry with command uvx and args mcp-server-motherduck, --db-path md:, and optionally --motherduck-token [E9][E14][E15]. Test the Configuration: Restart your IDE and run a test query: SELECT 1 AS test; If successful, the server returns the result, confirming the setup [E11]. SELECT mcp_publish_table('products', 'data://tables/products', 'json'); [E17] mcp_publish_execution_tool(name, desc, sql, props, required, bindings) - Publish execution tools with prepared parameter binding [E18]. Create a Rill project with curl https://rill.sh | sh and rill start my-rill-project, then ingest data from MotherDuck by configuring MotherDuck as a source and entering a SQL expression [E28][E40]. Generate an AI-powered dashboard in Rill via the side menu option "Generate dashboard with AI" [E30].

host can run multiple client instances.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP, spec 2025-11-25) defines three primitives for connecting AI models to external services: tools, prompts, and resources.

The DuckDB MCP server is distributed via the mcp-server-motherduck package. Install it using uv (preferred for Python CLI tools) or pip:
Install uv (Optional):pip install uv

Install the MCP Server:uv pip install mcp-server-motherduck

Or, with pip:pip install mcp-server-motherduck

The server acts as a bridge between DuckDB and AI-driven environments, such as Cursor or Claude, allowing these tools to execute SQL commands and return results in real time. It supports both local DuckDB instances and cloud-based MotherDuck databases, offering flexibility for diverse use cases. Additionally, the DuckDB MCP server includes security features like read-only mode and read-scaling tokens, ensuring safe integration with third-party tools.
This guide assumes you'll be using Rill's default embedded engine, DuckDB.
Rill Developer is an open-source, code-first BI tool that enables software engineers to profile data sets, design data models, and deploy dashboards to Rill Cloud.
At Rill, we’ve been longtime fans of DuckDB, in fact it’s the engine that powers auto-profiling and interactive modeling in Rill Developer, and the dashboards in Rill Cloud.

Users will follow the same basic steps that include
downloading and installing Rill 
 configuring MotherDuck as a source
entering a SQL expression to return a single table and clicking import
The DuckDB/MotherDuck MCP server allows the AI copilot (Cursor) to directly run queries against local DuckDB databases and/or remote MotherDuck databases and interpret the results.
Select the model's side menu and select "Generate dashboard with AI". Watch as Rill configures your metrics view and creates an Explore dashboard.

Each client is created by the host and maintains an isolated server connection:

Establishes one stateful session per server
Each client is created by the host and communicates with exactly one server:

Servers provide specialized context and capabilities:

Expose resources, tools and prompts via MCP primitives

Operate independently with focused responsibilities

Request client input (sampling, elicitation, roots) via InputRequiredResult within a reply

Must respect security constraints

Can be local processes or remote services

By default, Rill includes DuckDB as an embedded OLAP engine that ingests data from data sources and powers your dashboards. When you start a new project, you'll see a connectors/duckdb.yaml file alongside other project files. No additional configuration is needed to use DuckDB with Rill Developer or Rill Cloud.
Because Rill is already built with DuckDB embedded, no additional type wrangling is needed, the data in MotherDuck is “production-ready” for Rill dashboards.
Clients discover available prompts via prompts/list -- parallel to tools/list -- and present them to users as slash commands, menu items, or quick actions.
At the protocol level, a prompt is simple: the client calls prompts/get with a name and arguments, and the server returns a GetPromptResult containing a sequence of PromptMessage values.
